correctness.rationale: For every real inverse temperature and defect ratio in scope, exact heat-bath spin identities make the odd and even monomial sectors triangular, giving full generator decay rates and an explicit minimum of two positive branches. Their comparison at equal frustration, implicit differentiation on the weak-defect side, and positive derivative of the direct bond branch prove the unique optimum. The singular logistic boundary layer follows by explicit hyperbolic limits. The actual standalone verify.py was run on 64 rational activity pairs, checking all eight monomials in all eight configurations (4096 exact identities); finite checks are supplemental, not infinite certification.

originality.rationale: An exact eight-state signed-triangle heat-bath spectral gap with a unique opposite-sign coupling optimum and a logistic low-temperature window is not supplied by the inspected sources. The closest all-cycle monotonicity theorem explicitly assumes ferromagnetic bonds; antiferromagnetic chain works treat different Hamiltonians or dynamical observables. Published finding comparisons involve static Lee–Yang zeros, nonreversible bath switching, or discrete heat sweeps. An inaccessible six-spin paper and unindexed derivations create residual historical priority uncertainty, not identified stronger coverage.
residual_risks: Ismail–Salem 2003 full article was not accessible; only the publisher abstract describes a six-spin cluster. It might contain a hidden reduction or relevant limiting case.
Simple small-system diagonalizations or equivalent signed-spin gauges could have appeared in unindexed work. Current searches do not certify first publication.
Only the model and update normalization specified in the claim have been assessed; no novelty assertion is made for other Glauber conventions.

value.rationale: A frustrated triangle is the minimal simple cycle in which a negative bond cannot be gauged away. The complete sharp rate optimum extends the physical question of bond-strength monotonicity into a sign-frustrated system, exhibiting acceleration followed by slowdown. Its finite-window zero-temperature survival and explicit logistic crossover explain how competing energy barriers and degeneracy alter relaxation. The result is limited to a natural three-spin model, but it is not merely an arbitrary eigenvalue entry or a normalized restatement of a known ferromagnetic theorem.
